title: Regression: Prime Radiant Reporter readiness is stale
goal: Bug report: During T1303 protected deployment on 2026-07-16, production Prime Radiant /ready returned status=degraded with freshness.is_stale=true, max_age_seconds=530617, and latest_source_at=2026-07-10T21:20:42.490384Z. Expected: the previously Verified Reporter soup API reports non-stale acceptable readiness so Reporter can render /magazine and complete feed/delta/gap/ack. Actual: Reporter returned HTTPS 503, the production batch exited before writing artifacts or acknowledging, and T1303 rolled back. This is non-compliant with the T1304 readiness contract. Provenance must identify when and why production freshness stopped before any fix.
next_step: Code review R2 is active: distinct Codex reviewer session 019f6e01-2388-78a0-9658-72a873a01a13, model gpt-5.6-sol, high reasoning, read-only sandbox. Reviewer is checking the full hosted ticket/history, revision-4 contract, all prior findings, production fixture/live-Gibson proof, substrate/Reporter boundary, and full failure matrix. No deploy or T1303 owner contact before review passes and R1744-04 is proven.
notes:
R1744-01 provenance: commit 5144c68 introduced correct per-package durable ack gating, merged/deployed in 04b67aa on 2026-07-10; event 15163 succeeded at 21:20:42Z and event 15164 at 21:23:42Z became the first permanently unacked row. The later 6c01d190 Jul 13 deployment preserved this behavior.

R1744-02 boundary: TARS source DB, cursor query, package emission, SSH shipment, EURISKO service, and ack gating are healthy. EURISKO package consumption reaches LiveStoryAgentLoop meaning_update. The story_identity/meaning_update packet serializes all 663 tenant stories; meaning_update reaches about 130,884-130,925 prompt tokens in Qwen's 131,072-token context, leaving about 147-162 completion tokens. Truncated/malformed JSON raises before package persistence/ack, so correct cursor safety retains row 15164 and head-of-line blocks later material. T1670/T1721 are controlling product truth: repair prompt/context containment and failure observability. Do not decouple story-agent completion from T1654/T1656 durable package acknowledgement.

T1745 ticket-hosted implementation spec, revision 2

Goal: Restore fresh Prime Radiant production material without changing freshness/readiness semantics, durable package acknowledgement, or importing Reporter presentation policy.

Exact inference bounds:
1. Qwen context size is 131072 tokens. story_identity and meaning_update retain max_tokens=640. Before chat completion, LiveGibson must call the same Gibson llama-server /apply-template endpoint for the exact system/user messages with add_generation_prompt=true, then /tokenize that exact templated prompt. Invocation is allowed only when prompt_tokens + 640 <= 131072; therefore prompt_tokens must be <=130432. Tokenizer/template failure is a typed preflight failure and cannot acknowledge the package.
2. Retain the 180000-byte ceiling on the exact UTF-8 Jason-encoded user prompt object {instruction, output_schema, bounded_soup_packet}. Both byte and token limits must pass. Story synthesis keeps its existing separate 180000-byte budget.
3. LiveGibson computes prompt_bytes and prompt_tokens outside bounded_soup_packet. packet_bounds must not contain either value, avoiding recursive/fixed-point measurement. The returned success diagnostics and failed-report diagnostic carry both.

Bounded identity/meaning material:
4. For story_identity, replace rich whole-tenant visible_story_refs with a compact ACL-visible identity catalog. An eligible story is a non-quarantined story with at least one input visible to the actor under the existing input ACL check. Each compact ref is exactly {story_key, title, version, state, updated_at_story, last_material_at}; it excludes structural_facts and evidence_input_refs. story_key is retained in full; title is limited to the first 240 Unicode graphemes; scalar/time fields use their current values.
5. Rank every eligible compact ref by existing input/story token overlap descending with no minimum threshold, then last_material_at descending (nil last), then story_key ascending. The existing soup_candidate_hint remains separately present and advisory. Pack refs in that order until adding the next complete ref would violate either exact LiveGibson bound. This containment ordering is explicitly authorized as packet selection only; it does not decide identity, classification, or mutation. The model remains authoritative.
6. For current production, acceptance requires all 663 eligible refs fit and are included, so the retained row loses no viable current identity. Focused tests must prove the existing polluted-top-hint case still chooses forgotlings-ps5-launch while the hint is trump-israel-newsweek, and an existing correct story below the former ten-token hint threshold remains present and selectable.
7. For meaning_update, visible_story_refs is empty for a new story. For an existing identity-selected story, include exactly its compact ref as defined above; do not use the advisory hint to select it. meaning_update otherwise receives the current bounded source fields and authoritative story_identity result.
8. packet_bounds contains eligible_acl_visible_story_count (definition in item 4), included_story_count, omitted_story_count, and truncation_reason='live_story_agent_prompt_context_bound' iff omitted_story_count > 0. Source snippet remains its existing 600-character bound. The exact real row 15164 and an adversarial tenant with long titles and large rich story fields must both enter inference within byte/token bounds; rich fields excluded by items 4/7 cannot affect prompt size.

LiveGibson terminal diagnostics:
9. Successful chat completion requires choices[0].finish_reason exactly 'stop', binary choices[0].message.content, and a valid parsed JSON object. Missing or any other finish_reason, including 'length' or 'cancelled', is failure.
10. Success exposes response_id, finish_reason, provider usage prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/total_tokens (null only when provider omits them), preflight prompt_tokens, prompt_bytes, raw content_bytes, and content_sha256. content_bytes/hash are computed over raw returned content before think-block stripping or JSON extraction. AgentRun scope persists these fields and status remains succeeded.
11. Failed invocation intentionally creates no AgentRun because durable state is not written before package success. LiveGibson raises one typed terminal error for: template/tokenizer/preflight failure; curl/transport/nonzero exit; outer response decode failure; missing id/model/choice/content/finish_reason; non-stop finish; malformed inner JSON. Its single-line JSON diagnostic always contains stage, response_id or null, finish_reason or null, usage fields or null, preflight_prompt_tokens or null, prompt_bytes, content_bytes or null, content_sha256 or null, and error_class.
12. The existing TARS watcher <run-id>-failed-report.json error.message is the durable artifact for failed invocations and must preserve that complete one-line diagnostic. Tests inspect the failed report for preflight, transport, outer-decode, missing-choice, length, and malformed-content cases. No failure is reported as successful and the cursor remains unacknowledged.

Preserved invariants/non-goals:
13. Preserve source cursor/data, soup data, all-package durable ack gating, 86400-second freshness threshold, readiness status rules, feed/delta/gap/ack, and Prime Radiant/Reporter ownership. No Reporter code, consumer artifact readiness, cursor rewind, source/soup edit, Google RSS, backfill, watcher/LaunchAgent change, retry redesign, refusal fallback for malformed identity/meaning, unrelated validation, or legacy compatibility.
14. T1303 owner is not contacted before R1744-04. T1303 remains Deployable.

Add failed-report cases for every required missing field: id, model, choices[0], choices[0].message.content, and choices[0].finish_reason, in addition to preflight, transport, outer decode, non-stop finish, and malformed inner JSON. The story_identity and meaning_update model-visible bounded_soup_packet removes packet_id and contains packet_id_sha256 instead. packet_id_sha256 is lowercase hex over the same deterministic recursively key-sorted compact UTF-8 JSON encoding of the complete durable packet_id defined in item 15.
